{{Quote|Exactly as reported. A degree-six revolt, population equivalent to the Duros uprising on Zilior. Subjects occupy a moderate radius of jungle. Good, good&hellip;|Lord [[Drowl]]|<ref name="TOR:TG" />}}
Around [[3643 BBY]], during the height of the [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]], a group of [[Slavery/Legends|slaves]] on the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|reconstitued Sith Empire's]] [[Capital/Legends|capital]] [[Planet/Legends|world]] of [[Dromund Kaas/Legends|Dromund Kaas]] initiated a '''rebellion''' against their Imperial masters.

==Prelude==
{{Quote|So Darth Vowrawn is on the Dark Council. And his apprentice, Lord Qet, wants to advance, so he starts building a giant statue to his master. But Lord Qet doesn't want his master to know, so he brings in slaves from offworld. Slaves rebel, and we get this mess.|[[Vol Kolla]]|<ref name="TOR:SF" />}}
The slaves, brought to Dromund Kaas from offworld, were on the capital planet to build a [[Unfinished colossus|colossal statue]] in honor of the [[Dark Council]] member [[Darth Vowrawn]]. Commissioned by Vowrawn's [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]], [[Sith Lord/Legends|Lord]] [[Qet]], the statue was to tower over the surrounding jungle and advance the young [[Sith/Legends|Sith's]] career and reputation.<ref name="TOR:SF" /> Over the course of several [[Standard year/Legends|years]], the project faced repeated delays and accidents and saw the [[Death/Legends|deaths]] of hundreds of slaves. The harsh labor conditions and unforgiving demands of their masters eventually motivated the slaves to revolt&mdash;a rebellion that was in fact facilitated by [[Darth Baras]], a Sith Lord and rival of Lord Vowrawn.<ref name="TOR:PtP" /> The slaves armed themselves and seized the construction site as well as the surrounding jungle,<ref name="TOR:TUC" /> throwing off the yoke of slavery and declaring war against their former overlords.<ref name="TOR:RS" />

==The rebellion==
{{Quote|Lord Qet wants to save face, but secretly. He calls in me and my mercs. By the time we get here, the slaves have captured some giant industrial drills, and they're getting ready to bring down the whole giant statue. Our best team goes in with explosives to blow up the drills.... Slaves kill every last one.|Vol Kolla|<ref name="TOR:SF" />}}
[[File:Dromund_Kaas_slave_rebellion.jpg|thumb|left|280px|Imperial troops surrounding the [[unfinished colossus]].]]
In order to defeat this rebellion, the [[Dark Council]] summoned Lord [[Drowl]], a Sith experienced in quashing uprisings and revolts. Drowl used the slave rebellion as an opportunity to disperse his newly-developed [[Quell toxin]]&mdash;a poison that would [[Torture/Legends|torture]] the slaves and demoralize their comrades. Drowl utilized up-and-coming [[Sith apprentice/Legends|Sith apprentices]], [[Imperial Agent]]s, and [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]] to disperse his toxin and cripple the rebellion.<ref name="TOR:TG" /> While the Sith waited for the revolt to die down, Imperial [[Commander/Legends|commanders]] began to explore reports of murders in the slave camps. Upon further investigation, it was learned that a cult of Sith-worshipping slaves known as the [[Unchained]] had begun ritually killing their comrades as sacrifice to their masters.<ref name="TOR:TSK" /> The Sith ultimately decided to use The Unchained cultists to further their own purposes in the battle. The [[Captain/Legends|captains]] and commanders of the rebelling slaves eventually decided that they could best advance their own agenda by threatening to expose Darth Baras's hand in the contention. Baras, hoping to avoid the [[Politics/Legends|political scandal]], sent his [[Emperor's Wrath|apprentice]] to the foot of the colossus to kill the extorting slaves.<ref name="TOR:PtP" /> Despite the [[Unidentified Human (Dromund Kaas)|leader]] of the slaves being targeted and killed by an Imperial agent, later known as [[Cipher Nine|Cipher 9]],<ref name="TOR:TSS" /> the rebellion continued and Darth Vowrawn's colossal statue remained a battleground instead of a monument.
